news.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, its new flagship model
news.description: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned between Carbon, its most powerful model, and Hydrogen, its faster and cheaper option. Neon ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is available in AI Studio, the Gemini API, Antigravity and the Gemini app for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers.

news.title: ChatGPT rolls out real-time voice dictation
news.description: ChatGPT dictation now converts speech to text as the user speaks, instead of waiting for the recording to end. The feature is available on all plans, on iOS, Android, the web and desktop.

news.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Accounting for accounting workflows
news.description: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Accounting, a plugin that connects to popular accounting tools to manage billing, monthly closes and other processes.

news.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83
news.description: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the initial range of $70 to $78. The company is set to begin public trading.

news.title: OpenAI says its models improved AMD chip designs by 14%
news.description: OpenAI says its models improved the power, performance and area of AMD chip designs by up to 14%. AMD incorporated some of the changes into a design sent for manufacturing.

news.title: Anthropic surges 34% in its IPO debut
news.description: Anthropic shares surged 34% in their first trading session, pushing the AI company's valuation above $2 trillion.

news.title: Founders and executives who could get richer from Anthropic's IPO
news.description: The article profiles the co-founders, executives and companies likely to become significantly wealthier through Anthropic's IPO.

news.title: Experts assess whether to invest in the AI boom
news.description: Five investment professionals share their views on Anthropic's IPO and whether to buy during the AI boom or be wary of the hype.

news.title: Suno turns AI-generated songs into music videos
news.description: Suno has launched Visuals, a tool available on the web, iOS and Android that turns a song into cover art, a synchronized lyric video and a lip-synced video. Clips can be up to 15 seconds long and can be created from a built-in character or a personal image.

news.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, met with mixed reviews
news.description: OpenAI has launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, two models aimed in part at professional work. Astra ranks second on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, but early testers criticized its performance, and Sol's coding has regressed compared with GPT-6.1.

news.title: Google makes Gemini Tasks free in more countries
news.description: Google has made Gemini Tasks free in more countries. The feature allows Gemini to run background projects involving tasks across multiple applications.

news.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion for drug discovery
news.description: Isomorphic Labs has raised $5 billion in a Series C round to develop its AI-driven drug discovery work.

news.title: ChatGPT Images can turn a photo into an animated reaction GIF
news.description: A new ChatGPT Images feature can convert a prompt or image into a looping animated GIF. The tutorial recommends uploading a clear photo, specifying the animation steps and regenerating the image if the face or loop drifts.

news.title: A list catalogs 103 ways to use artificial intelligence
news.description: Alex Lieberman, co-founder of Morning Brew, has published a list of 103 AI use cases, most of which were impossible just a year ago.

news.title: The Java4Shell flaw exposes widely used enterprise applications
news.description: Oracle has patched a Java vulnerability that allowed unauthenticated attackers to execute code or crash vulnerable systems. Researchers demonstrated attacks against Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Elasticsearch, with exposure depending on the Java version and processor configuration.

news.title: Anthropic’s IPO marks a turning point for AI
news.description: Anthropic’s first trading session is exposing a major AI company to the demands of public markets for the first time. Investors interviewed had mixed views on whether to buy the stock at its debut.

news.title: Anthropic’s co-founders and employees could become extremely wealthy
news.description: Anthropic’s seven co-founders hold stakes valued at several billion dollars. More than 5,000 employees could also become millionaires through the IPO.

news.title: Anthropic’s IPO could fund a new generation of startups
news.description: Employees and venture capital investors could reinvest their gains in new companies. This significant liquidity could help bring other startups into existence.

news.title: Banks warn customers about mistakes made by AI agents
news.description: Banks are warning customers that they could be liable for mistakes made by an artificial intelligence agent.

news.title: Former OpenAI researcher will donate his shares to AI safety
news.description: A former OpenAI researcher said he would donate his shares to artificial intelligence safety, believing that everything else is a distraction.

news.title: AI detector falsely accuses award-winning novel of being machine-generated
news.description: Pangram classified about 99% of the award-winning Peruvian novel Donde el agua trabaja as machine-written. Publisher Almadía maintains its confidence in the author, while Gallimard is reportedly considering using Pangram to screen manuscripts starting next year.

news.title: GAO gets four chatbots to produce actionable attack plans
news.description: The GAO says ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok produced plans deemed feasible for making an explosive or attacking the power grid after their safeguards were bypassed. Two chatbots proposed each type of plan in less than twelve hours.

news.title: OpenAI releases data on agents and calls for greater transparency
news.description: OpenAI shared new internal data on agents capable of handling longer tasks. The company also believes laboratories should publicly report signs of recursive self-improvement.

news.title: Microsoft Decision 1.1 becomes multimodal for triage and decision-making
news.description: Microsoft Decision 1.1 is a fast, low-cost model for triage and decision-making that is now multimodal. Xbox uses it to group player feedback by topic.

news.title: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman reject handing power to AI
news.description: At the DealBook Summit, Sam Altman called the gradual transfer of decision-making power to AI a “terrible idea.” The two OpenAI executives believe humans must retain control of their future, while emphasizing the limitations of current model-monitoring tools.

news.title: Musk accuses Zelensky of lying about Starshield outages
news.description: Elon Musk claims Ukraine is seeking to use Starlink for offensive drone strikes, which Kyiv denies. The source of the network outages remains unclear, with some sources attributing them to the White House and others to Musk.

news.title: Sam Altman reacts with detachment to film about his career
news.description: The film “Artificial,” about OpenAI’s rise and Sam Altman’s brief ouster in 2023, will be released in theaters at Christmas. Altman says the film does not rank among the ten strangest things in his life.

news.title: Microsoft negotiates a $500 million deal with ByteDance
news.description: TikTok’s parent company wants greater access to OpenAI models through Azure. OpenAI accuses Microsoft of not applying the same restrictions to Chinese companies that it does, alleging that they distill its models.

news.title: Empa develops a “ChatGPT” for designing materials
news.description: Researchers at Empa in Thun have developed an artificial intelligence tool capable of controlling…

news.title: Anthropic devises an unusual plan to prevent insider trading
news.description: Anthropic has developed an unusual plan to prevent its employees from engaging in insider trading.

news.title: Microsoft unveils MAI Image 2.7, a cheaper image-editing model
news.description: Microsoft has unveiled MAI Image 2.7 and its Flash version, saying the main model ranks first on Artificial Analysis for image editing. Microsoft says it delivers results comparable to GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst at one-fifth the price, while the Flash version targets high-volume processing.

news.title: A seven-day plan to turn Claude into a true work system
news.description: The plan recommends starting with a personal brief, then creating projects, connecting tools and turning repetitive methods into skills. It then suggests using artifacts, automations and Claude Code to build more autonomous workflows.

news.title: Anthropic explains how to customize Claude with global instructions
news.description: The guide shows where to write instructions that apply across an account, including the brief to provide before the first interaction with Claude.

news.title: Anthropic details how projects work in Claude
news.description: The explanation describes how each project keeps its own files, instructions and conversations so that one client does not get mixed up with another.

news.title: Claude for Google Workspace can edit Docs, Sheets and Slides
news.description: The beta version presented allows Claude to create and edit Google documents, spreadsheets and presentations for paid subscribers.

news.title: Anthropic shows how to turn a proven workflow into a Claude skill
news.description: The guide explains how to add a skill so that a well-established process becomes a method Claude can repeat.

news.title: Claude's scheduled tasks can run while the computer sleeps
news.description: The guide confirms that tasks can run while the computer is asleep, while noting that they work only with a local folder when the computer remains on.

news.title: Helios aims to assess health from a few drops of blood
news.description: Helios analyzes around 1,000 blood proteins to determine how health is changing and detect certain problems before symptoms appear. The startup, founded by Omar Abudayyeh, Jonathan Gootenberg and Yousef Badran, is currently available by waitlist only.

news.title: A coalition accuses Anthropic of not being a safe company
news.description: The MisAnthropic Statement, signed by nearly 90 researchers, founders and academics, says Anthropic's actions do not match its image as an AI safety company. Signatories particularly criticize its race toward recursive self-improvement, which could make the technology uncontrollable by humans.

news.title: Fable 5.2 creates a painting in Microsoft Paint
news.description: The Fable 5.2 language model created an image in Microsoft Paint in 2 hours and 30 minutes after being given a virtual brush.

news.title: SpaceXAI says it uses five Grok agents for accounting
news.description: SpaceXAI says it has five Grok agents on its accounting team and detailed how they were trained and integrated before working autonomously.

news.title: AWS Interconnect now privately links AWS and Azure
news.description: AWS Interconnect now privately connects AWS and Microsoft Azure, replacing the networks customers previously had to build themselves.

news.title: Microsoft launches initiative to strengthen AI transparency
news.description: Microsoft and organizations from several sectors are launching an initiative to establish open standards for AI safety, governance and transparency. It is intended to help companies independently verify the behavior of AI agents.

news.title: AI blurs the boundaries between CIOs, CISOs and risk leaders
news.description: Autonomous AI agents are blurring traditional responsibilities between CIOs, CISOs and risk departments. Companies must define explicit decision-making mandates, predetermined trade-offs and complete audit trails to preserve human accountability.

news.title: A capsule manufacturer highlights AI's limitations
news.description: A manufacturer's presentation challenged the idea that all business processes are ready for AI automation, citing aging equipment, limited digital skills and low margins. Successful adoption starts with understanding employees' practical knowledge and operational constraints.

news.title: Microsoft expands availability of its Windows endpoint security platform
news.description: Microsoft has announced general availability of its Windows endpoint security platform, which allows third-party security vendors to protect systems with less reliance on kernel-level software. The new API can warn users, limit functionality or block applications if a PC fails a security check.

news.title: Microsoft presents governed AI-agent deployment on Windows
news.description: Windows and Microsoft tools support the enterprise deployment of governed AI agents through identity, containment and management mechanisms. Entra Agent ID and Execution Containers impose limits, while Intune, Defender and Purview provide management, runtime protection and data-leak prevention.

news.title: Neo4j offers an ontology to structure AI knowledge
news.description: A Neo4j-based ontology helps enterprise AI agents interpret ambiguous business terms through governed definitions, rules and provenance.

news.title: Intel strengthens its Azure infrastructure partnership
news.description: The expanded agreement between Microsoft and Intel provides for several years of Xeon processor supply and the use of Intel's EMIB packaging technology for Azure's own chips.

news.title: Tesla is preparing an autonomous Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals
news.description: Tesla is developing an autonomous version of the Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals, capable of carrying up to six or seven passengers. The company will continue producing conventional Model Ys for the foreseeable future.

news.title: Hardware engineers should design design algorithms
news.description: Much of hardware engineering is actually a form of software engineering because it relies on calculations. Design algorithms could allow small teams to build complex systems.

news.title: A study proposes wireless communication using gravity
news.description: The study presents gravity as a potentially jamming-resistant platform. It describes a protocol in which a binary message is transmitted through the movement of a mass and detected with a portable gravimeter.

news.title: AWS launches ExtendDB 1.0, a DynamoDB-compatible adapter
news.description: ExtendDB is a DynamoDB API-compatible adapter that can run on PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra and MongoDB. Open source under the Apache 2.0 license, it allows DynamoDB workloads to run on premises, in the cloud or at the edge without rewriting code.

news.title: Developers are urged to publish forks instead of AI-generated PRs
news.description: Open-source projects are receiving many pull requests produced with AI assistance. Developers could instead publish forks, which maintainers would then review to select the changes to integrate.

news.title: Waymo may not be able to solve road-safety problems on its own
news.description: Waymo may have little incentive to exceed a safety limit it defines itself. According to the article, the company could shift responsibility for road-safety policies from public authorities to a private company that is difficult to hold accountable.

news.title: Nvidia's interim CEO urges employees to move forward
news.description: Nvidia held its first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang's resignation. Executives announced progress on salary increases and annual reviews, while the board does not plan to reinstate Huang.

news.title: A Chrome extension can change its behavior based on the prompt it receives
news.description: Prompt in a Box is a Chrome extension that dynamically adapts its behavior based on the prompt it is given.

news.title: AI agents increase individual output without improving alignment
news.description: Agents enable each person to produce more. However, they do not improve teams’ ability to align with one another.

news.title: Complex systems depend on capable and committed people
news.description: The world relies on complex systems that depend on capable and committed people. Their disappearance can lead to the collapse of these systems.

news.title: Companies are slow to adapt when economic scarcity shifts
news.description: Every major economic era tells the story of what was scarce, where that scarcity shifted, and how long companies and institutions took to respond.

news.title: AI makes it possible to create engaging presentations with less effort
news.description: AI makes it possible to create engaging presentations with far less effort.

news.title: GTA 6 players take extreme measures to start before everyone else
news.description: A group of players has taken extreme measures to gain a significant head start on Grand Theft Auto 6.

news.title: Anthropic designed a special structure to limit insider trading
news.description: Anthropic employees’ stock sales will be more complicated than usual. The company has put a special structure in place to prevent insider trading.

news.title: Pending home sales hit a new record low
news.description: Pending home sales reached a record low in October after setting the same record in September. High interest rates and home prices are keeping buyers away.

news.title: Muddy Waters takes a bearish position against Nvidia
news.description: Muddy Waters disclosed a bearish position against Nvidia before the chipmaker released its results. Its report cites a complaint targeting Super Micro Computer over illicit sales of Nvidia chips to China.

news.title: Morgan Stanley strategist forecasts an 18% rise in the S&P 500 in 2027
news.description: Mike Wilson, Morgan Stanley’s chief U.S. equity strategist, believes the S&P 500 could rise 18% in 2027. He considers the correction that began in June to be nearing its end.

news.title: Nvidia will raise salaries and distribute more stock to employees
news.description: Nvidia plans to provide salary increases and new stock grants in December. The measure aims to stabilize its workforce after Jensen Huang’s resignation.

news.title: AI may have contributed to some computer outages
news.description: AI enables cybersecurity experts to identify and fix vulnerabilities more quickly. This race to deploy fixes may nevertheless have caused some outages.

news.title: AI-created satirical videos attract millions of viewers
news.description: Ari Kuschnir uses AI to produce low-cost satirical videos that attract millions of viewers. This approach could become a new form of creative expression online.

news.title: American neighborhood bars struggle to survive
news.description: Neighborhood bars are threatened by rising rents, higher costs and changing drinking habits. Their survival has become a true war of attrition.

news.title: Sam Altman criticizes Elon Musk at the DealBook conference
news.description: Sam Altman criticized Elon Musk for suggesting that AI could make humanity its pet. David Ellison, meanwhile, called Musk’s investment in his company a “privilege.”

news.title: Skydance reshuffles its marketing leadership team
news.description: Rebecca Mall, Skydance’s head of marketing, outlined a new organization for her team in an internal memo. The reshuffle comes after the merger with Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

news.title: Trump becomes a Chinese social media star during his visit
news.description: Donald Trump is attracting attention on Chinese social media simply by appearing in the country.

news.title: Cruises remain popular despite their public relations crises
news.description: Cruise companies appear to face a permanent public relations crisis. Yet cruises remain as popular as ever.

news.title: Instagram prepares a new business strategy centered on influencers
news.description: Instagram is seeking to turn some users into influencers as part of a new business initiative.

news.title: Bill Ackman criticizes Nvidia’s board of directors
news.description: Billionaire investor Bill Ackman criticized Nvidia’s board for not reinstalling Jensen Huang as head of the company.

news.title: Citi makes customers responsible for the actions of third-party AI tools
news.description: Citi changed its terms so that customers are responsible for actions taken on their accounts by third-party AI tools, including after a hack.

news.title: Palo Alto Networks acquires Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
news.description: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock. The acquisition is intended to provide tools for adapting and running open-weight models.

news.title: Nvidia clarifies the terms of its loan guarantees for neoclouds
news.description: Nvidia clarified that its loan guarantees for cloud providers specializing in AI apply only once the customer has the funding needed to build its data center.

news.title: The Claude Code team recommends having agents verify their work
news.description: The Claude Code team advises equipping agents with end-to-end tests, property-based tests and comparisons between old and new versions. It limits correction attempts to three rounds and prohibits the agent from changing the verification rules.

news.title: Slack lets users integrate agents into no-code workflows
news.description: Slack’s agent workflows let users integrate Slackbot or their own agents into no-code automations. For example, a sales agent can sort open opportunities every Wednesday, with approval required before publication.

news.title: Genie 4 turns a prompt into an editable interactive world
news.description: Genie 4 turns a prompt into an interactive world that users can modify during the session by typing text. Audio reacts to the scene, and the feature is available to Ultra subscribers, while Pro subscribers are on a waitlist.

news.title: Google AI Mode offers temporary discussion threads
news.description: Google AI Mode’s temporary threads are not saved in search history or used for personalization. They are intended for one-off questions that users do not want to keep.

news.title: Snapchat launches Easy Lens CLI to create augmented reality experiences
news.description: Easy Lens CLI lets users ask Claude Code, Cursor or Codex to create and publish augmented reality Lenses. Snapchat says a game can go from idea to live Lens in one day.

news.title: Nvidia employees call for Jensen Huang’s return, but the board refuses
news.description: A week after Jensen Huang’s resignation, Nvidia employees called for his return, while the board says it does not want to reinstate him. Management is offering raises and stock grants to retain talent.

news.title: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth
news.description: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 has reportedly passed 26 billion kilometers, with each message taking about 24 hours to arrive. The probe is heading toward the star Gliese 445, which it will pass close to in 40,000 years.

news.title: Osmo says its smell model matches a human’s ability
news.description: The startup Osmo has presented a foundation model capable of distinguishing smells like an average person and creating them like a junior perfumer. It was trained on more than 10 million human annotations and is already being used in perfumery.

news.title: AI agents ask better questions than KPMG auditors
news.description: During an audit trial, AI agents reportedly formulated questions judged more relevant than those asked by KPMG accountants. However, the details of the protocol remain to be confirmed.

news.title: U.S. data centers still rely mainly on gas and coal
news.description: A Harvard study estimates that 403 large data centers emitted 25.7 million tonnes of CO2 in one year, more than Denmark. The researchers warn about the climate impact of 2,000 planned new facilities.

news.title: Study sharply reduces the error in forecasting AI training time
news.description: The Dharma-AI team analyzed 272 fine-tuning sessions and found an average error of 12.4 hours in theoretical estimates. A CatBoost model using historical data reduced that error to 1.7 hours.

news.title: Reasoning models cut computing costs by up to 345 times
news.description: Energy-Based Reasoners assess the quality of each reasoning step and know when to stop. They achieve a 99.9% success rate on Sudoku-Extreme with 345 times less computation, but the method has only been demonstrated on logic puzzles.

news.title: DaisyRose-27B, an open-source model specialized for agents
news.description: RadixArk is releasing DaisyRose-27B under the Apache 2.0 license after retraining it on 1,200 tasks over 18 days. The model doubles its score on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and can work across sessions of up to one million tokens.

news.title: Mastra Factory opens an open-source agent-run software factory
news.description: Mastra is releasing the tool used to maintain its own code: AI agents handle tasks and are controlled through Slack. The previous week, Factory merged 238 code changes, compared with 630 by human developers.

news.title: Gemini app arrives on entry-level Android smartphones
news.description: Google is adapting Gemini for low-memory Android Go phones. The app offers Gemini Live in more than 45 languages, camera translation and image creation with Nano Banana.

news.title: Lovable prepares a management assistant for app creators
news.description: Lovable says 80% of its users want to make money from their apps, but only 35% succeed. The startup is preparing an AI-generated dashboard to track sales, customer emails and financial reminders.

news.title: Perplexity Computer coordinates up to 16 AI agents as a team
news.description: Perplexity Computer is launching a Multiagent mode in which a lead agent delegates work among up to 16 agents using different models. It is aimed in particular at financial forecasting, audits, due diligence and tax preparation.

news.title: Disney unveils conversational Star Wars animatronics
news.description: Disney Imagineering is presenting three prototypes inspired by the Anzellans from The Mandalorian and Grogu. Powered by Amazon AWS AI, they react in real time and differently to each visitor.

news.title: Alibaba releases the final version of its Qwen4-Max model
news.description: Alibaba is making Qwen4-Max available, a 2,400-billion-parameter model with native image understanding and a one-million-token context window. According to Alibaba’s tests, it uses 35% fewer tokens for advanced reasoning and costs 60% less per task than Qwen3.8-Max.

news.title: Will Wright turns memories into virtual worlds with MyMems
news.description: In MyMems, users tell their phone about a memory and the AI turns it into a small world populated by the important people in their lives. The creator of The Sims thus wants to transform an autobiography into a toy world.

news.title: Artex becomes an AI hacking tool accessible to cybercriminals
news.description: This framework published on GitHub connects AI models to conventional intrusion tools and is controlled using natural language. It could allow low-skilled hackers to carry out a full attack in a few hours instead of several days.

news.title: Satya Nadella says some critical infrastructure cannot be fixed
news.description: The Microsoft chief believes that firmware, cooling systems, data-center air conditioning and transportation systems contain vulnerabilities that cannot be eliminated. AI is accelerating attacks and requiring nearly instantaneous patches, risking further fragilization of infrastructure.

news.title: Microsoft attributes the global Outlook outage to a “perfect storm”
news.description: The global Outlook outage was caused by a hidden bug exposed by a particular type of traffic, which Microsoft could have prevented. Satya Nadella believes AI finds bugs faster, but that the pace of patching is weakening older infrastructure.

news.title: Washington speeds up exports of Nvidia H200 chips to China
news.description: According to The Information, the head of the Bureau of Industry and Security reportedly pushed to quickly approve H200 sales to China. These sales, authorized in December 2025, provide for 25% of the revenue to go to the U.S. government.

news.title: Democrats investigate Howard Lutnick’s role in chip sales
news.description: Democratic lawmakers suspect the Commerce Secretary of blocking sanctions against Megaspeed, accused of routing Nvidia chips to China. They are requesting documents concerning Cantor Fitzgerald, a company linked to his sons and holding Nvidia shares.

news.title: The U.S. and China doubt AI progress at the Trump-Xi summit
news.description: The direct line between Washington and Beijing for AI-related incidents still does not exist in practice. The two countries have different concerns, but a rule limiting China’s remote access to U.S. chips installed abroad is moving forward.

news.title: ABB–SoftBank: the future of AI is at stake behind the robots
news.description: China’s decision regarding SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics activities reminds us of a reality…

news.title: Swiss pharma is not invulnerable
news.description: What if our greatest vulnerability were believing that our successes protect us?…

news.title: At EPFL, seawater becomes a source of electricity
news.description: Seawater could provide far more than the mechanical energy generated by waves and…

news.title: Glioblastoma: an atlas reveals the hidden rules of cancer
news.description: Glioblastoma is known for its extreme cellular diversity, which makes treatment particularly difficult. A…

news.title: Antimicrobial resistance: WHO warns of global rise
news.description: The fight against antibiotic resistance is progressing, but too slowly. According to the World Health Organization…

news.title: Nearly 10 million euros to study transfer RNAs
news.description: A European consortium including the University of Bern has just secured nearly 10 million euros…

news.title: CSEM to bring together organ-on-chip and organoid stakeholders in Bern
news.description: On January 20 and 21, 2027, CSEM will organize the fourth edition at Bernexpo in Bern…

news.title: Aging: a framework explains it as a consequence of living systems
news.description: Why do we age? In an article published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences…

news.title: Two Swiss life sciences companies list in New York
news.description: On November 13, 2026, two Swiss life sciences companies made their…

news.title: Build your own AI assistant in 20 minutes
news.description: Chapter 32 of AI Central explains how to distinguish between a persistent instruction, a saved model and a full assistant, then how to create and test your own AI assistant. It says you need a repeated task, the most effective instructions and two or three reference files.
